title: gop evidence graph (gop.graph/v2)
description: graph.json written by gop collect. The Go source of truth is internal/graph/types.go. Unknown fields and attribute keys are allowed so additive changes stay within v2; consumers must ignore what they do not know.

audit_retention_days.description: Audit log retention (days) the audit facts were read under. When set, audit edges older than half of it are stale by default.

org_collected_at.description: Optional. When each org's facts were last read, keyed by org login (RFC 3339). A merge of a re-collection of some orgs into an older graph keeps the older time for the other orgs.

Evidence.description: How a fact was observed. inferred means derived from other observed facts by a documented rule (attrs.rule names it); it counts as confirmed. not_visible means unknown, not absent. supplied means read from a file the user supplied (a cloud OIDC trust policy); gop did not observe it live.

Attrs.description: Flat string attributes. Unknown keys are allowed.

attr_evidence.description: Per-attribute evidence where it differs from evidence.

NodeAttrs.description: Node attributes. Known keys are typed below; unknown keys are allowed.

ref_protected.description: action_ref on a branch: whether branch protection stops a pusher from changing it alone.

ref_protection.description: Comma list of the branch's rules, e.g. reviews,dismiss_stale,status_checks.

bypass.description: Comma list of principal IDs that can land code on the protected branch, or move the immutable tag, alone; none, or unknown.

ref_kind_source.description: action_ref: api when ref_kind was looked up, name when it is the name heuristic (a fallback).

ref_ambiguous.description: action_ref: the ref name is both a tag and a branch (ref_kind is then branch).

ref_immutable.description: action_ref with ref_kind=tag from the API: whether pushing alone cannot move the tag.

ref_immutable_reason.description: Why ref_immutable is true: an immutable release, or a tag ruleset with update and deletion rules.

token_write.description: workflow: whether its GITHUB_TOKEN has contents: write on its own repo (unknown when the default workflow permissions are not visible).

token_scopes.description: workflow: comma list of the token's other write scopes, e.g. id-token,packages, or write-all. Display only.

risky_triggers.description: workflow: comma list of its triggers that run in the base repo's context on events people without push access can cause (pull_request_target, workflow_run, issue_comment, ...).

actions_lock.description: repo: true when gop read a .github/workflows/actions.lock (gh actions-lock); unknown when one is listed but could not be read or parsed. Absent: no lockfile.

actions_access.description: Repo hosting a referenced action: its Actions access setting (who outside the repo may use its actions), public for public repos, or unknown.

source.description: Where the node's facts came from: the API label on an org found outside the enterprise listing; cartography on a cloud_target that a CAN_ASSUME edge from a Cartography export points to.

account.description: cloud_target: AWS account, GCP project or Azure subscription, when the trust file names it.

role.description: cloud_target: role name, GCP service account or Azure identity.

warnings.description: cloud_target: comma list of risk codes from the trust, e.g. no_sub_condition, no_aud_condition, wildcard_owner, unparsed_condition.

poutine_rules.description: workflow: sorted comma list of the poutine rule IDs with a finding in this workflow file (gop enrich --poutine). Cited from poutine, not proved by gop.

poutine_severity.description: workflow: the highest poutine rule level among those findings.

poutine_jobs.description: workflow: sorted comma list of the job ids the poutine findings name.

poutine_file.description: workflow: the poutine report the findings were read from.

advisories.description: action_ref: comma list of the OSV advisory IDs (GitHub Actions ecosystem) that affect this ref, e.g. a known compromise. Set only for affected refs.

advisory_severity.description: action_ref with advisories: the highest advisory severity.

advisory_fixed.description: action_ref with advisories: the first fixed version that leaves every listed advisory; absent when one has no fix.

EdgeAttrs.description: Edge attributes. Known keys are typed below; unknown keys are allowed.

rule.description: Inferred edges: the rule that derived the fact from other observed facts, e.g. default_perm, org_owner.

via.description: CAN_PUSH provenance, e.g. default_perm, org_owner, direct, outside_collaborator, team, ref_bypass, token_write, unknown (not_visible edges to repos gop did not collect). New values may be added within v2.

jobs.description: Comma list of job ids: those a via=token_write CAN_PUSH edge comes from, or those that can mint the token on an EXECUTES_WITH edge to oidc.

environments.description: EXECUTES_WITH to oidc: comma list of the id-token jobs' environment names; *dynamic* for an expression.

job_workflow_ref.description: EXECUTES_WITH to oidc: comma list of called reusable workflows that mint the token, as owner/repo/path@ref.

repository.description: EXECUTES_WITH to oidc: the token's repository claim, owner/repo.

repository_owner.description: EXECUTES_WITH to oidc: the token's repository_owner claim.

ref.description: Branch or tag a via=ref_bypass CAN_PUSH edge applies to.

file.description: Repo-relative path of the workflow or action file the edge was read from.

file_ref.description: Commit or branch the file was read at, when known.

trigger.description: CAN_TRIGGER: the risky trigger the principal can cause, e.g. pull_request_target.

exec.description: CAN_TRIGGER: how the workflow runs attacker input.

actions_lock.description: USES edge from a workflow in a repo with an actions.lock: locked when the lockfile pins it (and every nested ref gop saw), stale when it does not (counts as unpinned).

locked_sha.description: USES edge with actions_lock=locked: the commit the lockfile pins.

lock_entry.description: USES edge with actions_lock=stale: comma list of the lockfile's pin keys (owner/repo@ref) for the same action repo.

lock_missing.description: USES edge with actions_lock=stale: comma list of the nested refs (owner/repo@ref) the lockfile does not pin for this workflow.

lock_advisories.description: USES edge with actions_lock=locked: comma list of the advisory IDs that list locked_sha as affected. Describes the locked commit only; the action node's advisories attrs stay the ref-level match.

lock_advisory_severity.description: USES edge with lock_advisories: the highest severity among them.

lock_advisory_fixed.description: USES edge with lock_advisories: the first fixed version that leaves every one of them; absent when one has no fix.

consumer_org.description: USES edge into an enterprise-hosted action: org of the using workflow or action.

matched_sub.description: CAN_ASSUME: comma list of the trust's sub patterns that matched.

claims.description: CAN_ASSUME: comma list of the claims the trust checks.

pointer.description: CAN_ASSUME: JSON pointer of the trust inside the supplied file.

oidc.description: CAN_ASSUME: the oidc node whose token the trust matches.

reason.description: CAN_ASSUME with evidence not_visible: why gop cannot decide the match.

trust.description: CAN_ASSUME: the trust's own target when it names more than the cloud_target (an Azure federated credential).

source.description: CAN_ASSUME: cartography when the trust came from a Cartography export (gop enrich --cartography); absent for trust files.

observed_use.description: CAN_ASSUME: CloudTrail, through a Cartography export, saw a workflow of this repo assume the role.

times_used.description: CAN_ASSUME with observed_use: number of AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity calls in Cartography's CloudTrail window, integer as string.

last_used.description: CAN_ASSUME with observed_use: time of the last such call, as the export gives it.
